conditional_classification_chain: Assume A^alpha (equivalently A rtimes_alpha G, by Morita invariance) satisfies UCT.
The unital fixed-point algebra A^alpha is simple, separable, nuclear, stably finite and Z-stable, hence has finite nuclear dimension.
UCT gives quasidiagonal traces in the nuclear setting; Elliott-Gong-Lin-Niu machinery yields gTR((A^alpha) tensor Q)<=1.
Gong-Lin-Niu / modern Elliott classification classifies the unital fixed-point algebra by Ell.
Stable isomorphism then determines the stable isomorphism class of the crossed product. If G is finite, the crossed product is unital and the unital classification theorem applies directly.
exact_TR_note: Exact TR(A rtimes G)<=1 is not established here.
regularity_chain: TR(A)<=1 in the present simple nuclear stably finite setting supplies the regularity needed to place A in the Z-stable classification regime.
Fang-Tian Theorem 5.9 transfers tracial Z-stability to A^alpha.
Fang-Tian Theorem 5.11 gives Z-stability of A^alpha and A rtimes_alpha G for amenable/nuclear A.
Fang-Tian Section 4 gives simplicity and stable isomorphism (strong Morita equivalence) between A^alpha and A rtimes_alpha G.
uct_correction: Do not infer UCT(A^alpha) or UCT(A rtimes_alpha G) merely from UCT(A) and compactness/amenability of G. Preservation of UCT by arbitrary finite-group crossed products is strong enough to encode the general UCT problem (Barlak-Szabo / Barlak-Li). Stronger Rokhlin hypotheses have separate UCT-permanence theorems.
unitality_note: For an infinite compact group, A rtimes G need not be unital even when A is unital; use the unital fixed-point algebra for the standard unital Elliott invariant.
